notes.title: Lynleit
notes.text: Lynleit is likely to remain in command while other people are still in immediate danger, then feel the bodily violation of the attack once she reaches the trees. Her fury underwater fits both her childhood fear and her refusal to become helpless before something using human bodies as tools. The later complaint about the lost jacket can be concrete and mildly childish. She liked the garment, chose it for the operation, and had no chance to save it.

notes.title: Kyrien
notes.text: Kyrien is more likely to protect Lynleit by controlling what he says than by offering reassurance. His officer upbringing, private reserve, and Ti-led caution all support a literal answer that cannot be disproved. The restraint should not make him passive. He notices where she is exposed, where the official team has gone, and what his silence will cost if another authority learns the truth.

notes.title: Maren
notes.text: Maren is a trained officer, not a weaker swimmer. The horror lies in losing ownership of her own movement when hands seize her legs. Once ashore, a short sensory statement is more credible than a theory: she knows what fingers felt like, but does not claim to know who they belonged to. Anger or embarrassment at having needed to be hauled over the wall may surface after the immediate shock.

notes.title: Reiner
notes.basis: ISTJ with strong Si and Te
notes.text: Reiner's greater build makes him the practical anchor for Maren and Ivo, but the river prevents strength from solving the whole problem. He is likely to convert fear into tasks: secure the person, reach the wall, count the team, check the line. His later guilt would appear as stricter procedure and repeated equipment checks rather than a broad confession.

notes.title: Felix
notes.basis: ESFP with strong Se and Fi
notes.text: Remaining ashore should frustrate Felix because his most valued people descend without him. His role is still decisive. He keeps the cameras frozen, hears the failure before he can see it, abandons the van at the correct moment, and turns a communications fallback into a physical rescue line. A joke after the extraction can be an attempt to restore ordinary human rhythm, not proof that he took the danger lightly.
notes.chapterMatch: Felix left the van only when the operation had already collapsed.

notes.title: Blue flame under the river
notes.text: The blue flame can expose the scale of the horror without an explanation. Hands burning in blue beneath the surface would briefly illuminate different ages, sizes, and states of decay before the river closes over them again. The image would let the reader understand that Lynleit is fighting accumulated dead rather than a single submerged attacker.
notes.chapterMatch: Lynleit twisted downward instead of up.

notes.title: Lynleit
notes.basis: ENFJ with strong Ni, MSF duty primary
notes.text: Lynleit's concealed knowledge that Kyrien nearly harmed her gives the interrogation a personal edge, but she does not make the injury the purpose of the scene. Her MSF responsibility and anticipation of a larger threat remain decisive. The private anger should appear through unusually exact questions, controlled distance, or refusal to explain herself rather than flirtation or an emotional confession.

notes.title: Cards and physical tells
notes.text: Keep the games brief and embedded in operational downtime. Kyrien should win more often through technical play, while Lynleit gains ground by reading him. Their attention becomes sexual because hands, breathing, gaze, and proximity begin to distract them, not because either character starts performing romance. Lynleit notices the intrusion and returns to the mission.
notes.chapterMatch: The rematch continued on the third night.

notes.title: Kyrien
notes.basis: ISTP lean, officer ethics and autonomy
notes.text: Kyrien's decision to remain must occur when departure is genuinely possible and Lynleit's original authority has lost practical force. He is unlikely to explain the choice romantically. Staying, accepting the danger, and reopening contact are enough to separate voluntary loyalty from the vigilance of a coerced asset.

notes.title: Kyrien
notes.basis: ISTP lean, competitive drive and paternal inheritance
notes.text: The answer should remain immediate and unadorned. Kyrien does not reassure Lynleit or make her the reward because he experiences the fight as a chance to test himself. The useful ambiguity lies in what he does not examine: choosing a battle repeatedly places him beside the same woman, even while he continues to describe the motive as his own.

notes.title: The argument after Mikhail
notes.text: The argument remains about Kyrien exposing Felix and Reiner. Physical awareness belongs only in the delayed step apart and should not soften either position. Kyrien remains to help without apologizing, while Lynleit returns immediately to the institutional problem he has worsened.

notes.title: Lynleit
notes.text: The crying girl works as a lure because Lynleit notices a vulnerable person and assumes responsibility before she can test the situation. This does not require a general claim that women are more nurturing. Her Fe-oriented leadership, strong symbolic intuition, and experience of being watched make the trap personal. Afterward she may be angrier that the street used her protective instinct than frightened by the child herself.
notes.chapterMatch: She followed because a child was lost.

notes.title: Felix
notes.basis: ESFP with strong Se and Fi
notes.text: Felix experiences an ordinary physical emergency while Lynleit experiences the impossible street. His first response is immediate and tactile: get close, make noise, fan her face, check whether she responds. Once she wakes, his familiarity gives him room to tease, but affection should make him notice that her explanation is not a performance. He can believe that something happened without pretending to understand it.
notes.chapterMatch: His expression changed. The playfulness withdrew

notes.title: Helena
notes.text: Helena's grievance against Fionn becomes stronger if it includes the private humiliation of being treated as a wife in public and a security risk in his deepest life. Her response remains character-specific: she turns exclusion into a structural problem to remove. She is not dangerous because resentment makes her emotional. She is dangerous because she can organize resentment into policy, access, and succession.

notes.title: Fionn
notes.text: Fionn can sincerely believe that silence is a form of protection because his identity as father, husband, director, and Magiarch has trained him to equate love with containment. A masculine officer culture may reinforce the habit of carrying danger without asking family to share it. The flaw is not lack of feeling. It is his confidence that private endurance gives him the right to decide what everyone else may know.

notes.title: Yulia
notes.text: Yulia's decision to follow Hiyu into the park can contain two competing reactions: procedural disgust at the trespass and a familiar expectation that she will be the one who prevents his idea from killing him. As a young woman beside a reckless male friend, she may resent being pushed into practical responsibility while still choosing it. Her care appears in preparation, correction, and staying present rather than an open admission of attraction.

notes.title: Hiyu
notes.text: Hiyu's confidence in an elegant possibility may make the physical risk feel secondary until Yulia reacts to it. His eventual attachment should develop through dependence on the person who makes his ideas survivable. He does not need to become conventionally suave when desire appears. Confusion is more consistent if he recognizes that losing Yulia's company would be intolerable before he recognizes the feeling as romantic.

notes.title: Kyrien
notes.text: Directing MSF while Lynleit carries the Magiarchate forces Kyrien into a role built around speech, delegation, and institutional patience. His instinct may be to solve pressure alone because that resembles the officer ideal inherited from his father. A believable failure occurs when he withholds a burden that subordinates needed to understand, repeating Fionn's mistake in a different personality.

notes.title: Myka earns the outcome
notes.text: Myka's eventual first-place graduation should be earned through decisions she makes during the Academy crisis, not granted because Natalia and Kyrien rescue her. Their help can keep her alive or give her access, but at least one decisive discovery, refusal, or use of magecraft should belong to Myka alone and expose a weakness that follows her into MSF.

notes.title: Kyrien
notes.text: Kyrien's usefulness inside the Academy should come from seeing an ordinary operational pattern that trained Magi dismiss because they are looking for a magecraft explanation. His outsider status must also cost him: he cannot read magical danger directly and needs Myka or Natalia to interpret what his field instincts expose.

notes.title: Father Mikhail
notes.basis: XNJ lean, Church special envoy and confirmed counter-Magus field operative
notes.text: Mikhail's capability is strongest when the reader learns it through the decisions that keep him alive, not through a summary of techniques. Solitary endurance should expose what his Church training asks him to sacrifice, while at least one successful choice should become the reason Lynleit cannot dismiss his method as simple cruelty.

notes.title: Two effective methods
notes.text: The moral conflict should not make Lynleit naive or Mikhail a caricature. Each method needs to solve something the other cannot, and each needs a human cost the other recognizes. Their protection of one another remains professional and deliberate even while the disagreement makes later cooperation in Narvea harder.

notes.title: The jacket form
notes.text: The first time the leviathan-hide coat imitates Lynleit's lost suede jacket could occur when the resemblance is emotionally inconvenient. The form would turn an irritable complaint about clothing into posthumous evidence that Fionn noticed more of her ordinary preferences than his secrecy allowed him to say.

notes.title: Protection requires a choice
notes.text: The coat works best as protection with judgment rather than passive armour. Its need to be placed over a specific wound or person forces Lynleit to choose what she covers. Its autonomous form can inconvenience her, but the decision to protect remains hers.
